details: is an independent research laboratory, founded in 1935 and located in New Haven, Connecticut since 1970. Many current Haskins researchers are affiliated with Yale University's Child Study Center and/or the University of Connecticut. Haskins is a multidisciplinary and international community of researchers who conduct basic research on spoken and written language and global literacy. A guiding perspective of their research has been to view speech and language as emerging from biological processes, including those of adaptation, response to stimuli, and conspecific interaction. Haskins Laboratories has a long history of technological and theoretical innovation, from creating systems of rules for speech synthesis and development of an early working prototype of a reading machine for the blind to developing the landmark concept of phonemic awareness as the critical preparation for learning to read an alphabetic writing system.

explainer.lead: Haskins Laboratories is an independent research laboratory studying how people speak, read, and use language. Its work matters because it connects fundamental questions about human biology with practical ideas in speech synthesis, reading technology, and literacy.

tiers.eli5: Haskins Laboratories is a workshop where scientists figure out how the human language “engine” works. They study speaking and reading, then use what they learn to explore helpful ideas and tools. Their work includes machine-made speech, an early reading device for blind people, and the sound skills children need before learning to read.
tiers.practitioner: For an engineer, Haskins is best approached as a source of basic research rather than a software package or service. Its work informs speech synthesis, reading technology, and literacy research, while many of its researchers also have Yale or University of Connecticut affiliations. Historical prototypes and concepts from the laboratory should not be mistaken for current supported products.
tiers.paperLevel: Haskins Laboratories, Inc. is an independent, multidisciplinary research organization investigating spoken language, written language, and global literacy. Its guiding perspective treats speech and language as emerging from biological processes, including adaptation, response to stimuli, and conspecific interaction. Its contributions include rule systems for speech synthesis, an early working reading-machine prototype for blind users, and the landmark concept of phonemic awareness as critical preparation for reading an alphabetic writing system.

explainer.example: A child preparing to read an alphabetic writing system needs more than visual exposure to letters: Haskins’ landmark concept identifies phonemic awareness as critical preparation for learning to read.
